title: Rehearsal Before the Season
logline: A research lever opens two honestly labeled simulated pollock worlds, earning admiration for the ability to discover choices before those choices face a real fishing season.

cold_open.picture: Extreme close-up at rail height on a fictional researcher catching a chunky brass GearLever as a wet deck rolls; behind it the Eastern Bering Sea opens deep and wide. A tiny SIMULATION ONLY plate swings toward camera. The researcher is about to move a rule, not haul a fish.
cold_open.scroll_stop: The oversized small control against an immense ocean makes the opening question physically immediate.

escalation.draw: Researcher in Character worker outfit points the portable simulation control toward an inset wireframe sea; repeated season shutters open and close, explicitly illustrative, with no count. GearLever goes from parked to linked to model. The research capability gets the first full scene, with the question WHAT DID THE REHEARSAL EARN? planted at 16s.

escalation.stage: Wet laboratory with tank rims, plumbing, window and moving water reflections
escalation.draw: Same lever docks at CONSTANT RECRUITMENT detent. A top-down view shows independent unscaled CATCH and SPAWNING BIOMASS outcomes, their labels mounted to different tank rails. Constant inflow is a labeled schematic; do not animate exact numbers of fish as observed measurements.

escalation.stage: Wet laboratory, eye-level opposite side of tank
escalation.draw: Catch indicator pivots broadly between LOW and HIGH with SCHEMATIC / LARGE ANNUAL SWINGS fixed beside it. Separate biomass label reads HIGHER THAN COMPARISON with no bar lengths. A fresh unopened scenario port labeled STOCK-LINKED enters at 42s: will changing biology preserve the result?

escalation.stage: Wet laboratory doorway opening toward working harbor
escalation.draw: Lever fully lifts out of CONSTANT detent before docking at separate RICKER / STOCK-LINKED station. Comparison resets visibly. Two equal-size text windows state HIGHER CATCH and LOWER SPAWNING BIOMASS vs respective comparison. Camera travels through the door, carrying the actual lever in the researcher's hand.

escalation.stage: Harbor dock beside mooring posts, warehouse and actual water plane
escalation.draw: The lever makes one graceful schematic motion, then camera tilts to a season-calendar reel that stays unresolved: smoother policy response does not fill annual catch results. This pays secondary question at 73s by holding both experiments together: changing the assumption changes the tradeoff, and smooth control motion is not steady catch.

escalation.stage: Harbor dock, low waterline reverse toward researcher
escalation.draw: Real harbor extends beyond the little portable simulator. Three large empty sockets marked INCOME, BYCATCH and REAL SEASON refuse to light; researcher presents them plainly without grimace or invented victim. Lever remains connected only to the model. At 92s the primary reveal opens its previously folded plaque: ALTERNATIVES TO INVESTIGATE.

escalation.stage: Research vessel deck in matching opening composition
escalation.draw: Researcher returns the lever to TEST AGAIN while the entire real sea remains visible. The lever is useful and the ocean remains larger. Three goal labels appear one at a time in response to the closing question, never as an endorsement.

turn.earned_pivot: Research admiration survives its strongest limit: the simulator can propose alternatives worth investigating, while its outcomes remain dependent on assumptions and do not establish a winning operational rule.
turn.draw: The real harbor exceeds the model at a low-angle reveal; unmeasured income, bycatch and real-season sockets remain openly unfilled as the research plaque opens.

button.last_line: Which should a policy demonstrate first: steadier catches, more breeding fish, or a better balance across both?
button.last_image: Same brass lever from the opening rests at TEST AGAIN. The researcher turns toward the large real ocean, leaving all three goal labels equally legible.
button.loop_to_open: The opening asks what rehearsal can earn; the button keeps the research tool in use and makes the next test explicit.

sight_gags.gag: The wet-deck researcher cradles the small simulation control with both arms as if it were a huge catch, then discovers its dangling SIMULATION ONLY plate; affectionate joke about the outsized question, never a fake fishing result.

The unscaled annual-catch indicator swings far enough that a researcher must duck its rubber pointer; the independent biomass marker stays calmly labeled HIGHER, making the tension memorable without quantities.

The elegantly easing policy lever bows at the end of its move; an adjacent unresolved season reel declines to join the bow. Narration immediately separates smooth policy response from annual catch stability.

act3_test.name: The Harbor Is Bigger Than the Tank
act3_test.strongest_fair_case: Policy discovery might only reveal what the model rewards under its own assumptions. Neither scenario demonstrates a better real fishery outcome, stable income or bycatch performance.
act3_test.full_strength_drawing: Dedicate the whole harbor depth reveal to this objection. Display the Ricker biomass reversal at equal visual strength to the constant-case gain, distinguish smooth response from unproven catch stability, then show three unresolved outcome sockets against a real harbor. Never hide the test in a disclaimer.

throughline_object.object: One portable brass GearLever, adapted through existing color and longThrow parameters

states.state: Parked then connected solely to simulated sea
Lifted and reseated in separate STOCK-LINKED detent
Held beside unfilled real-outcome sockets, model cable visibly still attached
Returned to TEST AGAIN, plaque open as ALTERNATIVES TO INVESTIGATE

two_loops.name: What has the rehearsal earned?
two_loops.payoff: The withheld plaque opens to ALTERNATIVES TO INVESTIGATE after the full operational objection.

two_loops.name: Will changing biology preserve the result?
two_loops.payoff: Both labeled experiments are held together; stock-linked recruitment has higher catch and lower spawning biomass, and smoother response supplies no annual-stability result.

padding_test.verdict: A 90-second cut omitting the Act 3 test would be worse.

beat_tests.why_indispensable: The distinct Ricker result prevents generalizing the first scenario's biomass gain.
The smoother-response visual must be actively separated from annual catch steadiness, or a pleasing animation would assert unsupported benefit.
Unmeasured human and ecological outcomes bound what the discovered policy has established.
The delayed research payoff earns optimism after the objection; without it, the piece implies that non-operational research has no value.

vo_segments.text: What if you could rehearse a fishing rule before a real season? A new pollock study lets an AI learn through simulated seasons, then compares its choices with a predefined harvest rule.
The useful trick is discovering policies, not just predicting fish. But what, exactly, has the rehearsal earned? First, the model assumes constant recruitment: young fish entering the stock.

The learned policy leaves more spawning biomass than the comparison, alongside large annual catch swings. More breeding stock does not make those swings disappear. Now change the biological assumption.
In a separate experiment, recruitment depends on the stock. Here, the learned policy catches more and leaves less spawning biomass than its comparison. The tradeoff changes with the model.

Its policy response is smoother. That does not demonstrate steadier annual catches. And neither experiment establishes household income, salmon bycatch performance, or a winning rule for real fishing seasons.

That is the strongest test: a model can reward choices its own assumptions favor. These are illustrative simulations, with operational development still ahead. The rehearsal earns alternatives to investigate.
For Alaska, that is a useful place to start. Which should a policy demonstrate first: steadier catches, more breeding fish, or a better balance across both?

casting: Character worker rig; fictional illustrative researcher, no claim of stakeholder approval
Simulated/EvidenceState for model geometry and unresolved outcomes
Existing FX, biomes and stage3d materials where semantically correct
production.new_assets: At most a reusable portable scenario-control mounting frame; no salmon or trout rig relabeled as pollock. Use explicit unscaled schematic pollock paths if no vetted pollock asset exists.
production.freshness: Wet deck, tank parallax and harbor scale replace the last two office episodes; no Sheet, ReviewPen or credential hero.
evidence_rules: All experiment views visibly labeled SIMULATED.
Two recruitment scenarios reset and label their respective comparisons.
Qualitative labels and unscaled illustrative motion only; no invented quantitative graphs.
No policy smoothness claim becomes catch stability.
No income, bycatch, operational adoption or stakeholder sentiment is depicted as measured.
production.duration_rule: Executable build_scenes.py band112-130seconds applies to spoken read; credits append afterward. Target118seconds spoken,1secondtail,12.3secondscredits.

enthusiast_contribution: The affirmative accomplishment leads and gets a physical verb: researchers can discover candidate harvest rules through repeated simulated seasons. The final optimism is earned by keeping the tool useful after the strongest model-limit test.
